title: First Blood
tagline: All he wanted was something to eat.
about: A drifting Vietnam veteran gets run out of a small Washington town, and the sheriff keeps pushing until the woods push back.

    Off the LandHook-and-line pan trout with brown butter and almondsHook and line from the knife handle. Crisp-skinned trout, burnt butter, lemon.How to make it4 small rainbow trout fillets, skin on2 tbsp plain flour1 tbsp olive oil60g butter40g flaked almonds1 lemon, halved2 tbsp chopped parsleyPat the trout dry, season and dust the skin side with the flour.Fry skin side down in the hot oil until the skin is crisp, then flip for a minute and lift onto plates.Add the butter and almonds to the pan and cook until the butter smells nutty and the almonds are golden.Squeeze in the lemon, add the parsley and spoon over the trout.Smoked salmon and corn chowder in tin mugsDecember in the Hope woods. Hot-smoked salmon, potato, corn and cream.How to make it30g butter1 brown onion, diced2 celery sticks, diced2 tbsp plain flour400g potatoes, diced750ml vegetable stock250ml pouring cream2 corn cobs, kernels cut off250g hot-smoked salmon, flaked2 tbsp chopped dillMelt the butter and soften the onion and celery.Stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock and cream.Add the potatoes and corn and simmer until the potatoes are tender.Flake in the salmon, warm through, season with pepper and scatter with dill.Ladle into tin mugs and serve hot.Highway diner patty melts on ryeThe diner thirty miles up the highway. Beef, Swiss, slow onions, griddled rye.How to make it500g beef mince2 brown onions, thinly sliced40g butter, softened8 slices of rye bread8 slices of Swiss cheese2 tbsp American mustard1 tsp smoked paprikaCook the onions slowly in half the butter with a pinch of salt until soft and brown.Shape the mince into 4 thin patties the size of the bread, season with salt, pepper and paprika, and sear hard for 2 minutes a side.Butter the outside of the bread, then build each melt: cheese, patty, onions, mustard, cheese.Griddle the melts over medium heat, pressing down, until the bread is crisp and the cheese runs, then cut each into quarters.Smoked beef jerky and trail mix in a mess tinTrautman says he'll eat things that would make a billy goat puke.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Mess Tent MainsKnife-spear wild hog with charred apples and cider jusRambo spears a wild hog for supper. Fire-roast pork shoulder, apples, mash.How to make it1.8kg boneless pork shoulder (or wild boar), skin scored1 tbsp smoked paprika1 tbsp brown sugar2 tsp fennel seeds, crushed3 red apples, quartered2 red onions, cut in wedges250ml dry apple cider250ml chicken stock1kg floury potatoes60g butter125ml milkRub the pork all over with salt, the paprika, sugar and fennel, keeping the skin dry.Roast on a rack at 240°C for 30 minutes to blister the skin, then turn down to 160°C.Slow roast until a fork twists the meat easily, adding the apples and onions to the tray for the last 40 minutes.Rest the pork, then put the tray on the stove, add the cider and stock and boil, scraping, until syrupy.Meanwhile boil the potatoes, then mash with the butter and milk.Pull the pork into chunks and serve on the mash with the charred apples, onions and jus.After the BlackoutGas station blaze s'mores skilletThe gas station goes up in flames. Dark chocolate, torched marshmallow, graham crumbs.How to make it200g dark chocolate, chopped125ml thickened cream250g large marshmallows150g digestive biscuits, crushed40g butter, melted1/2 tsp sea salt flakesMix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter and salt and toast in a dry pan until golden.Warm the cream in a small cast-iron pan, take it off the heat and stir in the chocolate until smooth.Pack the marshmallows over the chocolate and grill or blowtorch until blackened in spots.Scatter the crumbs over and serve straight from the pan with spoons.From the ThermosFirst-light camp coffee with bourbon and mapleCome first light, every man on the ridge. Strong black coffee, bourbon, maple cream.How to make it750ml strong hot black coffee120ml bourbon2 tbsp maple syrup, plus extra to serve150ml thickened creamWhip the cream with a tablespoon of the maple syrup until just thick.Stir the bourbon and the rest of the maple into the hot coffee and pour into 4 enamel mugs.Float the maple cream on top and drizzle with a little more maple.Ice-cold cans of Rainier beerFor the deputies, once the search is called off.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
